# requireNonLength

<link-summary>Returns the value after checking that it is not a valid array-like length.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNonLength() — Returns the value after checking that it is not a valid array-like length. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNonLength<T>(
  value: T,
  message: string = "Expected a value that is not a valid array-like length."
): T;
```

A whole number from `0` up to `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` — the range a `length` property may hold.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                                            | Type     | Description                                                   |
| :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                                              | `T`      | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a value that is not a valid array-like length."` | `string` | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`T` — the same value, with a valid array-like length excluded from its type.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                               |
| :------------------------- | :-------------------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is a valid array-like length. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNonLength(-1); // => -1
requireNonLength(1.5); // => 1.5
requireNonLength(0); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNonLength(42); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
